newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt edges higher but trails strong U.S. bond.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt edges higher but trails strong U.S. bond.

text.p: Emerging debt prices inched higher Wednesday, but lagged behind a strong rally in the U.S. Treasury bond market, traders said.
"The half point move up in Treasury bonds was the only reason (for higher Brady prices)," one Brady bond trader said. "Our client flows have been pretty light. The (Brady) market is a bit apathetic."
Brady bond spreads widened agains the U.S. market, where the benchmark 30-year T-bond climbed 13/32 to yield 6.69 percent amid indications of benign U.S. inflation.
Argentina FRBs ARFLC05=RR rose 1/8 to 94-1/8, while Brazil "C" bonds BR8D14=RR gained 1/8 at 81-1/8 bid.
"Spreads were wider, that's probably a reaction to news of a lot of supply coming into our market," one Brady trader said.
Mexican Bradies continued to prosper from Tuesday's announcement that the country would prepay its $6.0 billion floating rate notes due 2001 that were backed by oil revenues.
"We're seeing demand for Mexico from investors," one dealer said. "Money needs to find a place. A lot of the money has been going into the long end."
Mexico pars MX625L19=RR climbed 3/8 to 78-1/2 bid, and the Mexico's global bond due 2026 MXUMS=RR gained 1/2 to 114-7/8.
In other news, Brazil's chamber of deputies approved a bill to regulate the telecommunications sector and privatize the federal phone company Telebras.
Also South Africa issued $500 million in 20-year debt at 183 basis points over, via Merrill Lynch.
